papers.title: Docker's tally card
lines: Call-on at the stands, seven sharp. Two hours' work, if you're lucky and your face fits.
Written below in biro: 'Our Paul got on the ship. Gone to Montreal. Mam says he'll be back for his tea.'

papers.title: Racing ticket
lines: Aintree, Saturday. Stand tickets, two. One for me, one for the horse's owner, who is a very good friend of mine.
The horse is called Wishful Thinking. We have both put money on it.

papers.title: Gig poster, handwritten
lines: The Cavern is NOT where we are playing. We are playing the church hall behind the chippy.
Doors seven, music half past, tea and a toasted teacake at the interval. Bring your own sandwiches.

papers.title: Label on a trunk
lines: To: Mrs M. Doyle, Sydney, New South Wales. From: her sister Kathleen, who is not coming after all.
Inside: three good towels, a rosary, and a note: 'You'll like it. The sun is free.'

trail.clue: Kathleen buried her own keepsake near the lamp post, 'where the ships can't see'.
